title: Lipoma and cyst removal
what: A surgeon removes a soft lump under the skin through a small cut, with local numbing. The tissue is usually sent to a lab to be checked under a microscope.
why: If the lump grows, gets in the way, hurts, becomes inflamed, or looks bad to you.
tell_doctor: If you tend to get thick scars
If the lump is red, hot, or painful right now. With inflammation, removal is usually put off

prepare.title: Check
prepare.text: First the surgeon examines the lump. Sometimes an ultrasound is done to see its size and depth.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: For a small removal, tests are often not needed. If they are, your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: On the day
prepare.text: You can usually eat. Take a shower and do not put cream on that area.

bring: Your ultrasound report, if you had one
steps: The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
Numbing injections are given, and the area goes numb
The surgeon makes a small cut
The lipoma or cyst is removed whole, with its capsule, so it does not come back
Stitches and a dressing are put on
The tissue is sent to the lab
feel: The numbing injections sting for a few seconds
After that, touching and pulling, but no pain
In the evening the area may ache
after: Keep the dressing dry and clean, as the doctor told you
No sauna or hard exercise for a couple of days
Stitches are usually removed after 7 to 14 days
The lab result comes in 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop when you press on it
Strong swelling, redness, pus, or a fever. These are signs of infection

faq.q: What is the difference between a lipoma and a cyst?
faq.a: A lipoma is a soft lump of fat tissue. A sebaceous cyst is a sac in the skin with thick contents. They are removed in a similar way.

faq.q: Can a fatty lump come back?
faq.a: If it is removed whole with its capsule, it usually does not come back in the same place. New ones can appear elsewhere.
